inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 59.006M cover-page count at 2026-07-31 (10-Q Q2 2026, dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding) plus 0.813M dilutive securities (Q2 2026 IncrementalCommonSharesAttributableToShareBasedPaymentArrangements) = 59.8M. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count). The Amazon customer warrants (up to 1.69M shares at $200.93, vesting on purchases through 2033) are NOT added to the count: they are contract consideration that will be recognised as a reduction of revenue, so their cost sits in the flows; treasury-stock-method dilution at strike ~= current price is <0.6% even at the bull-case value.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 10-K cash flow statement: share-based compensation add-back $49.947M plus taxes paid on net-share settlement of equity awards $14.284M (PaymentsRelatedToTaxWithholdingForShareBasedCompensation); Generac publishes no combined figure, so the two lines are summed. H1-2026 ran 27.4 + 36.7 = 64.1M (withholding spiked with the share price), which is why the FY2026 SBC% anchor is set above the FY2025 actual.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-09-25T20:00:02Z regular close (Friday); valuation dated the following Monday
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows discounted at a USD-built rate. Market WACC: 10-year UST ~4.2%, ERP 4.5%, 5-year beta ~1.35 (storm-cycle and AI-capex sensitivity) gives cost of equity ~10.3%; term loan B + revolver ~6.0% pre-tax, ~4.5% after tax; market weights ~92% equity / 8% debt on a ~$12.4B market cap against $1.28B debt -> ~9.8%, rounded to 10.0%. Explicit premium components (added 2026-09-28 after the multiples sanity check tripped): customer concentration +1.5% -- the September 2026 Amazon supply agreement (initial $2.4B, up to $8B, warrants vesting on purchases rather than take-or-pay volume) is roughly half the announced FY2027-28 pipeline, so the incremental value in every scenario rests on one counterparty; the low end of the skill's 1.5-2.5% range because the ~60% residential franchise (7,000+ dealers) carries no concentration. Small-cap illiquidity, regulatory and geographic premia: none (large-cap, NYSE, US-centric, no licence risk). Cyclicality: not stacked in the rate; it is charged in the scenario spread (bear margin trough 16%, bear weight 25%). WACC = 11.5%, one rate across all three scenarios.
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (A), leases as debt. Finance lease liabilities (~$90M) are already inside the CSV total_debt of $1,281M (LongTermDebt 1,212.5 + finance leases), so they are deducted once in the net-debt bridge and their principal is NOT deducted from the flows. Operating lease cost (~$52M liability) is a US GAAP operating expense already inside EBITDA; no adjustment.
inputs.nci_treatment: Negligible: non-controlling interest $5k plus redeemable NCI $0.37M at 2026-06-30; NCI share of H1-2026 net income -$0.4M. No leakage driver, no bridge item.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, cyclical industrial'), 10-year explicit horizon because margins and the data-center mix are still ramping through FY2029. Fresh build, first valuation of this ticker. (1) EBITDA basis: the margin paths are management's adjusted EBITDA (pre-SBC) basis, haircut ~0.5pt for the legal/regulatory/clean-energy/transaction charges Generac excludes most years; SBC is then charged separately via sbc_pct_path. FY2026 guidance of 20-21% includes ~1.5pt of one-off tariff refunds, so FY2027 steps down before the mix-driven ramp resumes. (2) FY2025 GAAP EBITDA in the CSV is $484M (11.5%) against the ~17% adjusted figure management cites; there is no extracted 10-K text to itemise the ~$180M non-SBC gap (operating income fell $248M on flat gross profit) -- flagged for the next refresh, it does not change the forward build. (3) FY2025 owner FCF of $204M is a trough (inventory build, capex step-up for capacity); the component build gives FY2026 owner FCF ~$430M, between FY2025 and FY2024's $530M, consistent with H1-2026 owner FCF of ~$89M on a seasonally H2-weighted cash cycle. (4) Working capital: a manufacturer with inventory 1,239 + receivables 669 - payables 556 = ~30% of revenue; wc_capture -15% credits hyperscale customer deposits and inventory normalisation for roughly half of that. (5) Cash tax 25%: GAAP ETR 24.6% in H1-2026; FY2022-25 cash taxes ran above book because of Sec. 174 R&D capitalisation and non-deductible acquired-intangible amortisation, both of which OBBBA expensing and the model's D&A convention (D&A path ~3.0-4.0% vs 4.6% reported incl. $102M amortisation) already lean against. (6) Buybacks: $147.9M in FY2025, zero in H1-2026 (cash went to Enercon, $212M net); the flat count is a funded convention historically, paused for M&A now. (7) Timing: year 1 is FY2026 discounted a full period while the balance sheet is at 30 June 2026; H1 owner FCF (~$89M, ~$1.5/share) is in both the cash balance and the year-1 flow, offset by the extra quarter of discounting. (8) Terminal cap 15x owner FCF (cyclical); at WACC 11.5% / g 3% Gordon (12.1x; bear 11.4x at g 2.5%) binds in all scenarios. The sanity check's EV/EBITDA exit caps (bear 9.6x = 10yr min, base 17.7x = 10yr avg, bull 29.6x = 10yr max) were tested and do not bind: the terminal EV/EBITDA is ~7.0x in the base, under even the bear cap, so the tighter owner-FCF cap is kept and the EV/EBITDA caps are recorded per scenario as terminal_cap_multiple_note. (9) Interest income not stripped: net-debt company, cash $265M vs FCF base $204M. (10) Sanity-check revision 2026-09-28 (same day as the fresh build): implied P/E 88.7x on trailing GAAP EPS tripped 2x the 10yr average (34.7x). The denominator is a trough -- FY2025 GAAP NI $161M with Q4 2025 GAAP NI negative, FY2025 GAAP EBITDA $484M vs ~$715M adjusted; TTM GAAP EPS through Q2 2026 is $4.41, and P/S (2.35x vs 2.75x avg) and P/B (3.75x vs 5.62x avg) were both below their 10yr averages at the prior IV. Two of the check's candidates were nonetheless under-charged in the build and are now applied: a +1.5% customer-concentration premium in the WACC (10.0% -> 11.5%) and a base-case FY2027-28 growth re-anchor (24%/14% -> 20%/12%, FY2028 revenue $7.1B -> $6.6B = top of the pre-Amazon Investor Day range). The 'growth_too_high 11.1%' candidate refers to historical_growth.selected_growth_rate (the 5yr revenue CAGR kept as PEG proxy), not the projection: the base 10-year revenue CAGR is now 6.9%, below the check's 10.3% through-cycle CAGR. Bull and bear driver paths are unchanged apart from the WACC.

historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5yr CAGR 13.7% diverges by more than 30% from EPS 5yr CAGR (-13.4%) and owner-FCF 5yr CAGR (-12.1%): book value compounded through the 2020-21 storm/COVID super-cycle while earnings and cash flow have since round-tripped (FY2021 EPS 8.51 -> FY2025 2.73). Neither series is a usable forward anchor; the projection is anchored to FY2026 guidance, the disclosed data-center backlog and the March 2026 Investor Day targets instead, and the revenue 5yr CAGR is recorded only as the PEG proxy.
historical_growth.notes: CAGRs on FY2020->FY2025 (5yr) and FY2022->FY2025 (3yr). Owner FCF series = reported FCF - SBC - equity-award tax withholding (interest income 0 throughout): FY2020 388.6, FY2021 218.3, FY2022 -98.1, FY2023 346.2, FY2024 530.5, FY2025 203.9. The 3yr owner-FCF CAGR is undefined because FY2022 owner FCF was negative (working-capital build). Owner FCF 5yr CAGR (-12.1%) is below reported (-8.8%) because SBC plus withholding tripled from $35.8M to $64.2M while cash flow fell: a rising share of the (declining) reported cash flow is being paid in stock.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +17% = midpoint of the maintained mid-to-high-teens guidance (H1 +11.5%, H2 carries Enercon and the data-center ramp). FY2027 +20% converts the contracted portion of the $1.35B data-center backlog scheduled for 2027 with residential high single digits, but takes only a small slice of the Amazon 2027-28 deliveries: the warrants vest on purchases, i.e. those volumes are not firm commitments, so they belong in the bull. FY2028 +12% lands revenue at ~$6.6B, the top of the pre-Amazon March 2026 Investor Day range of $6.2-6.6B. Thereafter the data-center cohort matures and growth fades to 2.5% by FY2035 (~$8.2B), a 6.9% 10-year CAGR, below the ~10% through-cycle revenue CAGR. (Revised 2026-09-28 from 24%/14% after the multiples sanity check; see valuation_philosophy.)
base.margin_rationale: FY2026 20.0%: guidance 20-21% less ~0.5pt for recurring 'non-recurring' charges. FY2027 19.8% as the ~1.5pt tariff-refund benefit rolls off against C&I mix and volume leverage. Ramps to 21.5% by FY2031, the bottom of management's 'low-20s by 2028' target, reached three years later and held: mid-cycle for a business that printed 24.5% in 2021 and 15.7% in 2023.
base.terminal_cap_multiple_note: Owner-FCF cap 15x; Gordon 12.1x binds. Sanity-check EV/EBITDA exit cap for the base = 10yr avg 17.7x; terminal EV/EBITDA here is ~7.0x, so it does not bind.

bull.growth_rationale: Top of FY2026 guidance, then the full 2027 backlog plus half the Amazon initial tranche ship on schedule (FY2027 ~$6.6B), Amazon exercises toward the $8B ceiling and further hyperscalers sign, taking FY2028 to ~$7.9B; residential holds high single digits on an active storm cycle and PWRcell attach. Growth fades to 3% by FY2034, ~$11.0B by FY2035.
bull.margin_rationale: Adjusted margin reaches the top of management's low-20s target (23.5%) by FY2030 as large-genset and switchgear scale plus Enercon synergies lift C&I margins toward residential levels; capex runs higher (4.8%) in FY2026-27 to build the capacity this path needs.
bull.terminal_cap_multiple_note: Owner-FCF cap 15x; Gordon 12.1x binds. Sanity-check EV/EBITDA exit cap for the bull = 10yr max 29.6x; terminal EV/EBITDA here is ~7x, so it does not bind.

bear.growth_rationale: FY2026 lands at the bottom of guidance. In FY2027 hyperscale deliveries slip and only part of the backlog converts (+10%); an AI-capex pause plus a mild storm season leave FY2028 at +3% and FY2029 at -3% as the data-center cohort is digested and residential reverts to its post-2021 pattern. Growth settles at 2.5-3%, ~$6.1B by FY2035 -- the 2022-style scenario where Investor Day targets are missed.
bear.margin_rationale: Tariff-refund benefit still lands in FY2026 (19.5%), then under-absorbed new capacity, price competition from Caterpillar/Cummins/Kohler for data-center awards and residential deleverage take the adjusted margin to 16.0% in FY2029 (FY2023 trough was 15.7%), recovering only to 18.0% -- the FY2024 level -- as capacity is right-sized.
bear.terminal_cap_multiple_note: Owner-FCF cap 15x; Gordon 11.4x binds. Sanity-check EV/EBITDA exit cap for the bear = 10yr min 9.6x; terminal EV/EBITDA here is ~6x, so it does not bind.

scenario_narratives.base: The residential franchise (~70-75% home-standby share, 7,000+ dealers) grows high single digits through the storm cycle while C&I grows strongly to FY2028 on the contracted $1.6B data-center backlog, taking revenue to ~$6.6B (the top of management's pre-Amazon Investor Day range) and the adjusted margin toward 21.5% -- the bottom of the low-20s target, reached late. Amazon volumes beyond a small slice are treated as bull-case upside because the warrants vest on purchases rather than committed volume. After FY2028 the data-center cohort matures: Generac is a scale supplier of gensets and switchgear to hyperscalers rather than the sole one, growth fades to GDP-plus and the terminal multiple is that of a cyclical industrial (Gordon 12.1x owner FCF under a 15x cap, ~7x EV/EBITDA). Hyperscaler concentration is charged as a +1.5% WACC premium; storm-cycle lumpiness and execution are priced in the scenario spread and weights.
scenario_narratives.bull: Generac becomes a structural AI-infrastructure supplier: the 2027 backlog and Amazon's initial $2.4B ship on schedule, Amazon exercises toward the $8B ceiling, further hyperscalers sign, and Enercon capacity lets C&I reach parity with residential by 2028 (~$7.9B). Scale in large gensets and switchgear lifts the adjusted margin to 23.5% by FY2030, and residential compounds on an active storm cycle, rising power prices and PWRcell attach. Even so, growth fades to 3% by the mid-2030s and the terminal value stays capped at a cyclical multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: The AI-capex cycle pauses in 2027-28: hyperscale deliveries slip, part of the backlog is pushed out or cancelled, and the concentrated customer base (Amazon) means the shortfall lands in one place. Residential simultaneously meets a mild storm season and a softer consumer, as in 2022-23. New capacity built for the data-center ramp is under-absorbed, competitors (Caterpillar, Cummins, Kohler/Rehlko, Eaton on switchgear) compete on price, and the adjusted margin falls to 16% before recovering only to the FY2024 level. Revenue reaches ~$6.1B by FY2035 -- roughly the pre-Amazon FY2028 target, seven years late -- and the March 2026 Investor Day targets join the 2022 ones as missed.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% house default to 25%: residential demand is storm-driven and lumpy, the Analysis JSON rates AI-capex cycle risk moderate-high, and management's previous Investor Day targets (2022) were missed by a wide margin when the cycle turned. Customer concentration (one agreement ~50% of the announced 2027-28 pipeline) is charged in the WACC as of 2026-09-28, not in the weight, so the 25% rests on cyclicality, execution and track record alone. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right at once: on-schedule hyperscale deliveries, capacity build without margin dilution, Amazon exercising beyond the initial tranche, and an active storm cycle. Base 50%: the 2027 backlog is contracted and the guidance track record through 2026 has been of raises, so the central case is the disclosed pipeline converting on a slower ramp than management's targets.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Owner-FCF DCF with SBC and equity-award withholding fully expensed, share count held flat, working capital charged on revenue growth (manufacturer, negative capture), a 10-year horizon so the data-center mix and margin ramp mature before capitalisation, and a 15x owner-FCF terminal cap (Gordon at ~12x binds; ~7x EV/EBITDA) because Generac is a cyclical industrial whose earnings round-tripped between 2021 and 2023. Discounted at 11.5% USD: a 10% market WACC plus an explicit +1.5% customer-concentration premium for the hyperscaler/Amazon dependence of the FY2027-28 step-up. Base case is anchored to the contracted backlog and the top of the pre-Amazon Investor Day FY2028 range (~$6.6B); Amazon conversion beyond a small slice is bull-case upside. Cyclicality and execution are charged in the scenario spread and a 25/50/25 weighting. House basis is the headline; the street (SBC-as-non-cash) basis is a memo.
key_risks_to_valuation: Hyperscale/AI data-center capex pause or delay: the FY2027-28 revenue step-up in every scenario rests on backlog conversion by a handful of customers; a slip moves value toward the bear case quickly.

Customer concentration: the Amazon agreement (initial $2.4B, up to $8B) is roughly half the announced 2027-28 pipeline; the warrants also make Amazon's purchasing partly self-interested rather than contractual.
Residential storm-cycle lumpiness: home-standby demand spikes and troughs with outage activity; 2022-23 showed how fast a 24% margin becomes 16%.
Execution in large-scale switchgear and power infrastructure against entrenched incumbents (Caterpillar, Cummins, Eaton) and the risk of under-absorbed new capacity if demand slips.
FY2026 margin guidance includes ~1.5pt of one-off tariff refunds; tariff policy and commodity (steel, copper, battery cell) costs can move margins either way.

Adjusted-EBITDA basis: Generac excludes legal/regulatory/clean-energy charges most years; the model haircuts 0.5pt but a larger recurring gap (FY2025 GAAP EBITDA was ~5.5pts below adjusted) would lower every scenario.
Working-capital intensity (~30% of revenue): a faster ramp than modelled consumes more cash than the -15% capture assumes unless hyperscale deposits are larger than expected.

sanity_check_revision.trigger: scripts/sanity_check.py: implied P/E 88.7x on trailing GAAP EPS exceeded 2x the 10yr average (34.7x); P/B 3.75x, EV/EBITDA 24.9x and P/S 2.35x were inside their bounds.
sanity_check_revision.diagnosis: Mostly a denominator artefact -- FY2025 GAAP EPS ($2.73, Q4 negative) is compressed by ~$180M of non-SBC charges and $102M of acquired-intangible amortisation, and TTM GAAP EPS through Q2 2026 is $4.41 (on which the prior IV was ~37x). But two of the check's candidates were genuinely under-charged: hyperscaler customer concentration sat in the scenario weights rather than the discount rate, and the base case front-loaded Amazon volumes that the warrant structure shows are not firm.
changes: WACC 10.0% -> 11.5% in all three scenarios: +1.5% explicit customer-concentration premium (Amazon agreement ~50% of the FY2027-28 pipeline; low end of the 1.5-2.5% range because the residential dealer channel carries no concentration). Weighted IV effect -$34.11/share.

Base FY2027 growth 24% -> 20% and FY2028 14% -> 12%: FY2028 revenue re-anchored from ~$7.1B to ~$6.6B, the top of the pre-Amazon Investor Day range; Amazon conversion moves to the bull case. Weighted IV effect -$3.21/share.

Not applied: mid-cycle FCF rebuild (FY2025 owner FCF of $204M is a trough, not a peak; year-1 owner FCF ~$390M sits between FY2025 and FY2024's $530M). Not applied: a per-year growth cap at the 10.3% through-cycle CAGR (the FY2026-27 growth is guidance and contracted backlog; the base 10-year CAGR of 6.9% is already below it). Not binding: EV/EBITDA exit caps of 9.6x/17.7x/29.6x -- the terminal EV/EBITDA is ~7x under the existing 15x owner-FCF cap.

Unchanged and deliberately so: margin paths, SBC/D&A/capex/tax paths, working-capital capture, 25/50/25 weights, bull and bear growth paths, 15x terminal cap. Evidence that would move them: FY2026 results showing the tariff-refund benefit is recurring (margins), a firm take-or-pay amendment to the Amazon agreement (base growth and the WACC premium), or a Q4 2026 GAAP-to-adjusted gap that persists (margin haircut).
sanity_check_revision.result: Weighted IV $162.09 -> $124.77 (-23%); the implied P/E on the check's trailing denominator falls to roughly 68x, inside the 2x bound, while P/S (~1.8x) and P/B (~2.9x) sit well below their 10yr averages. The dashboard should read the valuation as deliberately conservative on the multiples that use trough GAAP earnings.
